issues.claim: G123's new §2.6 step 7 says the plan in force stands — 'the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the building's built band and era (the as-built plan, below …)'. V03 §3.11 *Decay re-cuts no plan* (b) (J-V3.137), the volume that builds and draws the plan, re-derives an unstored plan 'at the occupant inputs it held in the week before its run began … the plan the building was last lived in, which for a building never re-let is its as-built plan'. They differ for every building re-let or re-banded before it was left: under §2.6 the plan a user saw is replaced at abandonment by the as-built layout — 'redrawn as new', against item 123's owner words and §2.6's own 'the plan in force stands'. And §2.8's elaboration record (the home of the plan rung's inputs and stale triggers) still lists the households housed, the occupants' band and value and 'its running Works' stage' as inputs and stale triggers with no decay-run exception, while V03 §3.11 and V03's lifecycle row (l. 302: 'no stale mark, §2.8') say the leaving stales nothing and a `decay` or `repair` Works is no build stage — V03 cites a §2.8 rule §2.8 does not state.
issues.required_change: (1) §2.6 step 7: replace '— the plan in force stands, the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the building's built band and era (the as-built plan, below; V03 §3.11's vacant re-cut is a standing building's only) —' with '— the plan in force when its decay run began (V06 §3.23 (1)) stands: the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the occupant inputs it held in the week before that run began (V03 §3.11 *Decay re-cuts no plan*: the plan it was last lived in, its as-built plan (below) when never re-let); V03 §3.11's vacant re-cut is a standing building's only —'. (2) §2.8, `ElaborationRecord.inputs`, the plan rung: 'its running Works' stage at the drawn week (item 67 (j))' → 'its running build Works' stage at the drawn week (item 67 (j); a `decay` or `repair` Works is none, §2.6 step 7)'; and in the `stale` sentence, after 'a dossier event of items 18, 22 or 31;', add 'for a building in a decay run (V06 §3.23 (1)) its occupant inputs — use, assignment, sub-locations, concealed use, the households housed and the occupants' band and value — are those of the week before its run began (V03 §3.11), so neither the leaving nor a later move of the field stales its plan;'.

issues.claim: §2.6 step 7 restates the decay level and its comparison (R2-38 (3)–(4)'s summary words) against their homes. Level: §2.6 reads it 'from its existence state, the years since the week of the epoch whose op set it `abandoned`' and gives V11's default age to 'a building with no abandonment epoch (generated ruined; first met in item 113's replay)'; V06 §3.23 (1)–(4), the level's home (R2-38 (3)), starts the decay run at the effective week (V06 §2.11) of the lifecycle event that took the building from a standing state into `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` — a `vacate`, a fire's `burn`, a flood's or a topple's `ruin` — and keeps the default age for a building with no decay run in the log. So a building a fire burns or a flood ruins, or one a hand edit abandons between epochs, ages from that week in V06 but sits at the default age under §2.6. Comparison: §2.6 calls 'level ≥ t' 'the one comparison every reader makes', while §6.3 *Plan damage* (the thresholds' home) shows an element damaged 'exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t — a level of 0 damages nothing'; V11's ranges admit lo = 0 (T-V11-47), so an element can draw t = 0 and §2.6's comparison damages it on a standing building, against §2.6's own 'a building never decayed (level 0) draws byte-identically' (`item123.damage`).
issues.required_change: §2.6 step 7: replace 'the building's **decay level** — V06's `decayLevel(doc, lineage, week)` in [0, 1], derived and never stored, from its existence state, the years since the week of the epoch whose op set it `abandoned` (its lifecycle events, §2.8) and V11's rate by material (timber faster than stone), read at the drawn week (§2.9's `week`) — shows damaged every element whose t it has reached (level ≥ t), the one comparison every reader makes.' with 'the building's **decay level** — V06 §3.23's `decayLevel(doc, lineage, week)` in [0, 1], derived and never stored, from its decay run (from the effective week, V06 §2.11, of the lifecycle event that took it from a standing state into `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` — a `vacate`, a `burn`, a `ruin`; its lifecycle events, §2.8), its state and V11's rate by material (timber faster than stone), read at the drawn week (§2.9's `week`) — shows damaged every element whose t it has reached while above 0 (level > 0 and level ≥ t; §6.3 *Plan damage*), the one comparison every reader makes.'; and 'A building with no abandonment epoch (generated ruined; first met in item 113's replay)' → 'A building with no decay run in the log (generated abandoned, decayed or ruined; first met so in item 113's replay; V06 §3.23 (4))'.

issues.claim: The round-2 support step (3) (VEW-r1-03, R2-26 (c)) makes the wall's band the support where a course crosses an enceinte: 'the wall carries the deck there — a … raised gate, whose tower carries the deck, or the curtain under an aqueduct's arch … that station's support `ring` is the band's stretch under the deck, the wall's own masonry (no pier raised …)'. That stretch stays on the enceinte's condition profile, which item 114's writers break: V06 §3.7.7 (2) breaches stretches in chain order (neglect, poverty, both low) and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` names any stretch; V06 §3.7.6 (5) holds the stretch only against V06 §3.7.2 (2)'s dismantling while the deck stands (a landfall is defined: V05's table breaches the wall and ruins the span and support it covers). No text says what a decay breach of the band under a standing deck does — the deck keeps a station whose support is 'a gap with rubble', or its spans merge across it past the clear-span bound; neither the support step, the span rule, V06 §3.7.7 nor V06 §3.19 defines it, and no bar covers it (T110-2 builds the crossing; the item-114 group decays rings with no raised way). Principle (11): walls decaying into gaps × a raised way carried by the wall, opened by this round's crossing station.
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after 'the clear-span bound reads the spans on either side of that station (T110-2)', add: '; while the deck stands, the stretch of the band under a crossing station is held by it — `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay pass over it in chain order as V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s dismantling does (it may wear, and a repair writes it as any run), a landfall over it breaching it and ruining the deck there by V05's landfall table — and from the first epoch after the raised way is removed or the spans on either side fall it is an ordinary run'; V06 §3.7.7 (2) cites it (V06's end); §13.2's item-114 group gains the fixture (scope's end): a neglected, poor CITY ring over 20 epochs with a masonry aqueduct through its wall arch and a viaduct on a raised gate — the stretch under each crossing station never `breached` or `dismantled` while its deck stands, every other stretch decaying as T114-1 states.

issues.required_change: §4.3: 'its two ends are ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices, or an end on the arena's outer ring with neither (§2.7's `RaisedFoot`; *At the frame*) — each of its two feet a vertex on part 0 …'; §4.6: 'a raised way's two ends (§4.3) are ramps or stairs by the same rule, but an end on the arena's outer ring, where none is drawn (§2.7's `RaisedFoot`)'.

issues.claim: G122h's §2.9 *The crisis framing* says 'Only the opening view, Fit and the limit change'. §9.5's *Framing* circle is both the initial view and the default export frame, and §9.5 widens that circle while a look stands; §8.7 cuts every export frame to the bounds of town and camps. §2.7's *Readers* line restates V06 §3.7.7 (3): 'patches rebuilt oldest first by the week of each run's `conditionEpoch` — its `EpochRecord.week`, so a replay epoch's patch before every live one's (§6.1) —, ties in chain order'.
